subject: Clarify non-training commitment + retention scenarios for logs & caches
messages:
From: Amy Bishop <amy.bishop@orionhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Orion Health Security <security@orionhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: Do you train on customer data? retention rules for logs & cache

Hi Sofia,

Quick question from our security and procurement teams as we evaluate Redwood for a clinical routing/triage pilot. Two related items we need clear answers on before proceeding:

1) Non-training assurance: We need an explicit statement of whether Redwood uses customer-provided content (prompts, inputs, uploads, or generated outputs) to train or improve shared models. Does Redwood ever incorporate customer data into model training or downstream model updates?

2) Retention/exception details: We have several data classes (PHI in payloads, ephemeral request/response traces, cached KV/embeddings used to speed inference). For each of the following, what are the default retention windows, and what controls do we have to shorten/disable retention?
  - API request & response logs (including headers but excluding bodies when possible)
  - Full request/response bodies used for debugging (if enabled)
  - KV cache / session cache (for multi-turn state kept on the service)
  - Stored embeddings (if a customer stores embeddings via the API)

We also need direction on how deletion requests are handled (time to purge, proof of deletion) and whether those deletion operations are visible in audit logs for our SOC2 evidence.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if easier — our team is in PDT.

Thanks,
Amy Bishop
Senior Security Manager | Orion Health

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>
To: Amy Bishop <amy.bishop@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: Do you train on customer data? retention rules for logs & cache

Hi Amy — thanks for the detailed list. TL;DR: Redwood does not use customer-provided production data to train our public/shared models; we provide configurable retention controls and a documented deletion workflow. Below are concrete answers mapped to your bullets, plus a few implementation notes.

Non-training commitment (short answer)
- Redwood does not include customer production data (prompts, files, or outputs sent to the hosted API) in model training or re-training of our shared models. That includes telemetry slices derived from production traffic. We maintain a formal non-training commitment for customers which can be contractually embedded (attached).

Retention and controls (defaults + options)
- API request & response logs: default retention 14 days for hosted API request/response logs used for routing/metrics. These logs can be shortened via account settings or disabled for Dedicated/Private environments. Logs exclude customer file payloads by default unless debugging is enabled.

- Full request/response bodies for debugging: retained 30 days when debug capture is explicitly enabled for a support incident. Debug capture is off by default; enabling requires an opt-in with a ticket and explicit justification. We redact credentials by policy during any capture.

- KV/session cache: session state (short-term KV cache to preserve context) is ephemeral and kept for the duration of the session plus a configurable grace window. Default grace window is 24 hours for hosted customers; Dedicated customers can set this to 0 or a custom TTL. Private/on-prem deployments give you full control — no Redwood-managed retention unless you enable it.

- Stored embeddings: if you store embeddings in Redwood’s managed index product, default retention is 90 days for accounts that do not actively manage indices (primarily staging/test accounts). For production accounts, embeddings persist until explicitly deleted by the customer or managed via lifecycle policies; we offer lifecycle APIs to programmatically purge vectors.

Deletion process and proof
- Deletion requests: open a support ticket or use the deletion API. For hosted customers, deletion operations are queued and typically completed within 48 hours; we provide a deletion confirmation token and an audit entry showing which object ids were removed.

- Audit evidence: deletion operations and their confirmations are recorded in the platform audit log. For customers on an enterprise contract (Dedicated/Private) we can provide longer retention of audit events or an export feed into your SIEM.

Attachments and evidence
- Attaching our one-page non-training commitment and a retention matrix that maps data classes to defaults and controls. I’ve also attached a SOC2 summary we can share with your security team; we can facilitate access to our full SOC2 report through the secure portal if needed.

If helpful, we can convert these bullets into contract language for procurement. I’ve cc’d Priyom (privacy) and Neha (security ops) — they can add details on deletion proof and SIEM integrations.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
redwood-inference.com

Note: Attachment stubs: redwood-non-training-commitment.txt (text), redwood-data-retention-matrix.pdf (pdf), SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Amy Bishop <amy.bishop@orionhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Orion Health Security <security@orionhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: Do you train on customer data? retention rules for logs & cache

Sofia — thanks for the quick and thorough reply. A couple of clarifying follow-ups from our security lead:

1) "Not used to train shared models" is helpful; can you confirm whether any internal research experiments (e.g., small-shot fine-tuning or evals) ever make use of redacted or aggregated customer telemetry? Our policy team wants a strict boundary: customer production data should not be part of internal model experimentation without explicit written consent.

2) For KV/session cache: if session context is persisted for 24 hours, could an administrator accidentally snapshot that state for debugging and thereby create a durable copy? Essentially: what safeguards prevent debug operations from escalating into longer-lived storage?

3) We will need the exact contract language (preferably short clause) we can push to our legal team and a timeline for SOC2 portal access.

If possible, please have Priyom or Rishi put the legal clause in an email reply so our procurement can paste it into the SOW. Thanks.

—Amy

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood-inference.com>
To: Amy Bishop <amy.bishop@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: Do you train on customer data? retention rules for logs & cache

Hi Amy — thanks for the follow-ups. Below are precise, copy-ready items you can share with legal/procurement. Happy to jump on a call if you prefer.

Contract language (suggested clause):
"Redwood Inference represents and warrants that Redwood will not use Customer Data (as defined below) to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood’s public or shared machine learning models, including internal experimentation, without the Customer’s prior written consent. For clarity, Customer Data does not include aggregated, de-identified telemetry that cannot reasonably be re-associated with the Customer.

Customer Data means: (i) content submitted by the Customer to Redwood’s inference endpoints, (ii) files uploaded to Redwood-managed storage, and (iii) any derivations of (i) or (ii) that are capable of re-identification to the Customer.
"

Safeguards for debug and cache handling:
- Debug captures require explicit opt-in via a support ticket; debug artifacts are tagged as "incident-debug" and are only accessible to a limited ops group for a time-limited window (default 30 days) and additional safeguards (RBAC + MFA) are applied.
- Administrative processes disallow escalating debug captures into permanent storage: any snapshot intended for engineering review must be approved by a second approver from security and marked for deletion by a deadline.
- For Hosted accounts with the 24-hour session grace window, session data is stored in a volatile cache backed by an ephemeral store. Snapshots are only taken if a debug capture is requested; otherwise the cache is not materialized to persistent blob storage. Dedicated/Private customers may opt out of all debug captures and set session TTL to 0.

SOC2 portal access:
- We can grant secure, read-only access to our SOC2 artifacts via the portal within 3 business days of a completed DPA/RO agreement. I’ve attached the SOC2 summary; portal access instructions will be provided once procurement requests the share link.

Proof of deletion and audit feed:
- Deletion API calls generate a confirmation token and an audit entry. For enterprise customers we offer a scheduled audit export to your SIEM (S3, Splunk, or direct Syslog).

We’ll also drop a plain-text non-training commitment file for signature (attached).

Best regards,
Priyom Das
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood-inference.com

Attachment stubs: redwood-non-training-commitment.txt, redwood-data-retention-matrix.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf
